data.gender_notes: Arnab is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arnab is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘arnava’, which means ‘golden’ or ‘eagle’. This name is associated with strength, courage, and the ability to soar above challenges. In Hindu mythology, Arnab is believed to be the name of a mighty eagle-like creature. The name Arnab carries the meaning “Golden, Eagle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arnab usually hope their child will grow to embody golden, eagle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength and courage, soaring above challenges.
data.etymology: Arnab belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Golden, Eagle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arnab total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

modern_usage.modern_context: Arnab is a popular Indian name known for its association with prominent news anchors, journalists, and TV personalities. The name Arnab is synonymous with dynamic and thought-provoking news coverage, making it a household name in the Indian subcontinent and the Gulf region. Some of the most notable figures bearing this name include Arnab Goswami, the founder and editor-in-chief of Republic TV (formerly with NDTV and Times Now), and Arnab Bhattacharya, a news anchor for ABP News. Arnab's modern context extends to various digital and print media as well, demonstrating the versatility and adaptability of this name within the journalism industry.
